facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus was a stegosaurian dinosaur that lived during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage in China.
facts.quote: Gigantspinosaurus () is a genus of stegosaurian dinosaur from the Late Jurassic (Oxfordian) Upper Shaximiao Formation of China.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus was a moderately sized dinosaur reaching up to 4.2 meters in length.
facts.quote: It was a moderately sized member of the group, measuring up to 4.2 m in length.

facts.statement: The first Gigantspinosaurus fossil was discovered in 1985 by Ouyang Hui and initially misidentified as Tuojiangosaurus in 1986.
facts.quote: The first fossil was found in 1985 by Ouyang Hui at Pengtang near Jinquan and was reported upon in 1986 by Gao Ruiqi and colleagues, mistaking it for a specimen of Tuojiangosaurus.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis was formally named by Ouyang in 1992 based on a lecture abstract.
facts.quote: The type species, Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis, was described and named by Ouyang in 1992 in an abstract of a lecture.

facts.statement: The genus name Gigantspinosaurus combines Latin words for 'enormous' and 'spine' to describe its gigantic shoulder spines.
facts.quote: The generic name is derived from Latin gigas or giganteus, "enormous", and spina, "spine", in reference to the gigantic shoulder spines.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus was widely considered a nomen nudum until 2006, when it was confirmed that the original abstract contained a valid description.
facts.quote: The name was generally considered a nomen nudum in the West, until in 2006 it was disclosed that the abstract contained a sufficient description.

facts.statement: Public awareness of Gigantspinosaurus grew in 2006 after Tracy Ford published a reconstruction article treating it as a valid taxon.
facts.quote: Public awareness of this animal was increased in early 2006 when Tracy Ford, considering it a validly established taxon, published a short article on reconstructing it.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen ZDM 0019 was found in the Upper Shaximiao Formation of Zigong, Sichuan, dating to the Oxfordian stage.
facts.quote: The holotype, ZDM 0019, was found in layers of the Upper Shaximiao Formation of Zigong (Sichuan province), which date to the Oxfordian.

facts.statement: The holotype consists of a partial skeleton of a likely subadult missing the skull but retaining lower jaws, hind feet, and the tail end.
facts.quote: It consists of a partial skeleton of a probably subadult individual missing the skull (though the lower jaws are present), hind feet, and the tail end.

facts.statement: In addition to bones, fossil plates, spines, scutes, and a skin impression on the left shoulder have been found.
facts.quote: Apart from skeletal elements also plates, spines and scutes have been found. At the left shoulder an impression of the skin had been preserved.

facts.statement: A second specimen, ZDM 0156 consisting of a pelvis, was reported in 2005 from Chenjia near Fuquan.
facts.quote: In 2005 Peng e.a. reported a second specimen, ZDM 0156, a pelvis found at Chenjia near Fuquan.

facts.statement: Peng and colleagues described Gigantspinosaurus as a medium-sized stegosaur.
facts.quote: Gigantspinosaurus was described by Peng and colleagues as a "medium-sized stegosaur".

facts.statement: Estimates place Gigantspinosaurus between 4.2 and 7 meters in length and weighing around 700 kilograms.
facts.quote: It is estimated to have been about 4.2-7 m in length and 700 kg in weight.

facts.statement: The neck plates of Gigantspinosaurus were small and triangular in shape.
facts.quote: The plates on the neck are small and triangular.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus likely had a relatively large head with thirty teeth in each lower jaw.
facts.quote: The head must have been relatively large with thirty teeth in each lower jaw.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus had very broad hips and a fused plate formed by the neural spines of the sacral vertebrae and the first tail vertebra.
facts.quote: The hips are very broad and the low neural spines of the four sacral vertebrae and the first tail vertebra have been fused into a single plate.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus possessed robust forelimbs.
facts.quote: It also had robust forelimbs.

facts.statement: A 2018 redescription classified Gigantspinosaurus as an intermediate basal stegosaur sharing traits with both huayangosaurids and other stegosaurs.
facts.quote: A 2018 redescription by Hao et al clarified aspects of the anatomy and found that it was an intermediate basal stegosaur, sharing basal traits with huayangosaurids as well as somewhat more advanced traits with other stegosaurs.

facts.statement: Analysis found that Gigantspinosaurus was not the most basal stegosaur, as huayangosaurids like Chungkingosaurus and Huayangosaurus were considered more basal.
facts.quote: Nevertheless, this analysis found that it was not the most basal stegosaur, as the huayangosaurids Chungkingosaurus and Huayangosaurus were considered more basal.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus lived approximately 156 million years ago during the Late Jurassic Oxfordian stage in what is now Asia.
facts.quote: que vivió a finales del período Jurásico, hace aproximadamente 156 millones de años, en el Oxfordiense, en lo que hoy es Asia.

facts.statement: The first fossil was found in 1985 by Ouyang Hui and reported in 1986 by Gao Ruiqi, who initially confused it with Tuojiangosaurus.
facts.quote: El primer fósil fue encontrado en 1985 por Ouyang Hui en Pengtang cerca de Jinquan y fue reportado en 1986 por Gao Ruiqi y sus colegas, confundiéndolo con un espécimen de Tuojiangosaurus.

facts.statement: The type species Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis was described and named by Ouyang in 1992 in a conference abstract.
facts.quote: La especie tipo, Gigantspinosaurus sichuanensis fue descrita y nombrada por Ouyang en 1992 en un resumen de una conferencia.

facts.statement: The generic name derives from Latin words for 'enormous' and 'spine', referencing the gigantic shoulder spines.
facts.quote: El nombre genérico se deriva del latín gigas o giganteus, "enorme", y spina, "espina", en referencia a las gigantescas espinas del hombro.

facts.statement: Public recognition of Gigantspinosaurus increased in early 2006 when Tracy Ford published a reconstruction article treating it as a valid taxon.
facts.quote: El reconocimiento público sobre este animal creció a principios de 2006 cuando Tracy Ford, lo consideró un taxón válido establecido, publicando un artículo corto sobre su reconstrucción.

facts.statement: Ford suggested that previous reconstructions showing shoulder spines pointing down were incorrect, proposing they extended upwards above the animal's back.
facts.quote: Ford sugirió que las reconstrucciones anteriores de Gigantspinosaurus donde muestran las espinas del hombro hacia abajo están incorrectas y su nueva reconstrucción muestra la espina algo hacia arriba, terminando más arriba que la espalda del animal.

facts.statement: The holotype ZDM 0019 was found in the Upper Shaximiao Formation of Zigong, Sichuan, dating to the Oxfordian.
facts.quote: El holotipo, ZDM 0019, se encontró en capas de la formación Shaximiao Superior de Zigong, provincia de Sichuan, que se remontan al Oxfordiano.

facts.statement: The holotype is a partial skeleton of a likely subadult missing the skull but including lower jaws, hind feet, and the tail end.
facts.quote: Consiste en un esqueleto parcial de un individuo probablemente subadulto que falta el cráneo, aunque las mandíbulas inferiores están presentes, las patas traseras y el extremo de la cola.

facts.statement: Besides skeletal elements, plates, spines, scutes, and a skin impression on the left shoulder have been preserved.
facts.quote: Aparte de los elementos esqueléticos también se han encontrado placas, espinas y escudos. En el hombro izquierdo se había conservado una impresión de la piel.

facts.statement: In 2005, Peng and colleagues reported a second specimen, ZDM 0156, which is a pelvis found at Chenjia near Fuquan.
facts.quote: En 2005, Peng y colegad informaron de un segundo espécimen, ZDM 0156, una pelvis encontrada en Chenjia cerca de Fuquan.

facts.statement: Peng and colleagues described Gigantspinosaurus as a medium-sized stegosaurian.
facts.quote: Gigantspinosaurus fue descrito por Peng y sus colegas como un "estegosauriano de tamaño mediano".

facts.statement: Gregory S. Paul estimated in 2010 that Gigantspinosaurus was approximately 4.2 meters long and weighed 700 kilograms.
facts.quote: Gregory S. Paul estimó que en 2010 tenía aproximadamente 4,2 metros de largo y 700 kilogramos de peso.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus has a distinctive appearance with small dorsal plates and greatly enlarged shoulder spines twice the length of the shoulder blades.
facts.quote: Gigantspinosaurus tiene una apariencia distintiva con placas dorsales relativamente pequeñas y espinas del hombro muy agrandadas, las espinas parascapulares, dos veces la longitud de los omóplatos, sobre los que descansaban a través de grandes bases planas.

facts.statement: The neck plates of Gigantspinosaurus were small and triangular.
facts.quote: Las placas en el cuello son pequeñas y triangulares.

facts.statement: The head of Gigantspinosaurus was likely relatively large with thirty teeth in each lower jaw.
facts.quote: La cabeza debe haber sido relativamente grande con treinta dientes en cada mandíbula inferior.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus had very broad hips and fused neural spines from the sacral vertebrae and first tail vertebra forming a single plate.
facts.quote: Las caderas son muy anchas y las espinas neurales bajas de las cuatro vértebras sacras y la primera vértebra de la cola se han fusionado en una sola placa.

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus had robust forelimbs.
facts.quote: Las extremidades anteriores son robustas.

facts.statement: A study by Maidment indicates that Gigantspinosaurus is the most basal known member of Stegosauria.
facts.quote: Un estudio realizado por Maidment indica que Gigantspinosaurus es el miembro más basal conocido de Stegosauria.

facts.statement: A 2018 redescription by Hao et al found Gigantspinosaurus to be an intermediate basal stegosaur sharing traits with huayangosaurids and other stegosaurs.
facts.quote: Una redescripción en 2018 por Hao et al aclaró aspectos de la anatomía y descubrió que se trataba de un estegosauriano basal intermedio, que compartía rasgos basales con huayangosáuridos, así como rasgos algo más avanzados con otros estegosáuridos.

facts.statement: The genus Gigantspinosaurus was named by Ouyang in 1992.
facts.quote: PBDB name: Gigantspinosaurus (genus), Ouyang 1992

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus belongs to the family Huayangosauridae.
facts.quote: Parent group: Huayangosauridae

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus is classified within the dinosaur class Ornithischia.
facts.quote: Class: Ornithischia

facts.statement: Gigantspinosaurus lived between 168.2 and 161.5 million years ago during the Bathonian and Callovian stages.
facts.quote: Time range: Bathonian to Callovian (168.2 to 161.5 million years ago)

facts.statement: There is currently only one recorded fossil occurrence of Gigantspinosaurus.
facts.quote: Fossil occurrences recorded: 1
